Decide the task shape for region-limited circuits: the interface already allows a narrower inRange (Option C, zero library lines), but a region task is a weaker trusted statement and each region needs its own Spec.lean. Either keep the full-range fdivP task for D1/D2 only and treat third-party circuits as proof-interface demonstrations, or add separate region tasks (drewbabel: 2<=W, 2<=P<=2^(W-1); HardFloat: 3<=W, 2<=P<=2^(W-2)+3), with a rule for ranking them.

Spend one Lean acquisition on a pure tooling probe: run sv_structure? on the evaluators' flat files (drewbabel fdiv_flat.sv at several (W,P), HardFloat hf_fdiv2.sv, fontamsoc fdiv32_flat_mul/flat_arr, Kemet fdiv32r.sv, the preprocessed tt_fp8). Nobody ran Lean, so fragment acceptance and the n^2 tactic cost for these netlists are unknown. Record the first refusal for each.

Land H3 gate 1 first (our own D2 proof and shared parametric math layer), and measure D2's sv_structure cost. Every third-party parametric proof reuses that layer; if the tactic cost stays about n^2, drewbabel's smaller flat (about 44 assigns vs D2's about 90 sites) is the hedge.

Make drewbabel fp_div_sqrt (unrolled flat, hypothesis P<=2^(W-1)) the first third-party proof target. It is parametric, covers W=2, shares the restoring-plus-RNE architecture with our reference, and is the smallest flat. Caveats to state in the task: young repo (2026-08-29, 1 star, own random testbench), the combinational form is the evaluator's rewrite so the theorem is about the rewrite, and the FSM-to-unroll equivalence is empirical.

Add Phy-Engine's original fp16_div_unit as a real-world negative test for tests/fdiv16 (counterexample a=0x07ff, b=0x4000, got 0x0000, want 0x0400, 60 failing pairs of 2^32 that random post-synthesis vectors miss), and keep the patched, flattened version as a second binary16 structure. Check first that the default-assignment variant loads through load_design_sv2, and that Apache-2.0 attribution is acceptable.

Archive the independent cross-checks as spec/oracle validation evidence: DGrid and TEA exhaustive at binary16, Kemet at about 26G binary32 pairs, drewbabel and HardFloat across formats up to (11,53). Optionally run D1/D2 against the drewbabel and HardFloat RTL at large formats we cannot exhaust.

Decide whether to invest in word-level `/` and `%` support in the tactics plus a fourstate rule for run-time division by zero (the quotient step then reduces to Nat.div_add_mod). This is the most common real-world idiom (Kemet, DGrid, TEA, rafi, Sherpa bf16) and would open a variant task without the `/ %` ban. Weigh against area: Yosys-lowered `/` costs 2142 GE versus 1930 for a hand restoring chain at binary16.

If a cheap demonstration of a fixed-format circuit at a new (W,P) is wanted, prove a flat DIV-only (4,4) rewrite of tt_um_fp8_fpu. The input space is 65,536 pairs, but decompose the proof rather than one exhaustive decide.

Treat HardFloat as the second region family: use the evaluators' hf_fdiv2.sv for differential testing at W>=3 and large formats first, and attempt a proof only after the drewbabel flat proof, because it needs a recoded-exponent math layer nothing else in the repo uses.
Re-run the (8,24) pinned scoring on an idle machine so binary32 baselines exist (the pinned scorer timed out under load 100-230 for Kemet, drewbabel, HardFloat, Sherpa, fontamsoc and fudian).

Do not pursue now: fudian (Chisel not runnable, unreliable region), Sherpa and fontamsoc (need `*`, a Newton error bound over 2^23 divisors, and a GPL concern for fontamsoc), FloPoCo and the toy fp16/bf16 dividers (non-conforming), and the NR/Goldschmidt estimate-only designs (not correctly rounded).

Only if the maintainers want a relaxed task: first measure rafi-1st FpDivUnit (parametric, combinational, `/` `%`, canonical qNaN sign 0, flush-to-zero; read but not measured, rounding unconfirmed) as the one clean flush-to-zero candidate. Most other relaxed designs differ on NaN policy, rounding, or format at the same time, so one relaxed spec would not cover them, and a new trusted spec function is needed.

Before copying any third-party file or derived rewrite into the repository, get a licence review: DGrid and TEA have no licence, fontamsoc is GPL-2.0-only, drewbabel's Solderpad wraparound and fudian's Mulan PSL v2 are unreviewed. The evaluators wrote all derived files only in the scratchpad.
